There is a sense of order in how everything is arranged. The buildings sit cleanly on the property, the traffic lanes are clearly marked, and the flow of vehicles has a rhythm that makes the whole operation look effortless. Even on busy days, the activity feels controlled rather than chaotic.

What stands out most is the purposefulness. These are not buildings meant to draw attention. They are built to support the movement of goods, the work of logistics teams, and the constant flow of products that keep businesses running. [{"Name":"Clint Eatherton","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjVJnjEjoHhcCFOMqS7IzdKzz_qlg0Yck0-dR4mn2bt_HF5AeIFsAA=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":1,"Description":"I do not leave negative reviews as a rule.  I generally just don't go back or I don't bother utilizing the service any longer.

BUT..... Lile Moving and Storage and their unethical business practices, need to be exposed and brought to light and protect/warn others.

Lile Moving and Storage uses deceitful tactics by low balling (after a full onsite inventory) only to charge you almost 20% more at delivery.  Yes I know it was non binding.

ZERO changes in the amount to move from inventory to move.  We actually had less furniture and clothing from when the inventory was done.

I've had 14 van line moves in the last 25 years and I've never had such a terrible experience.

Stay very far away from Lile Moving and Storge and use anybody else.  I thought I was using a reputable company, but I was wrong.

Communication was great until I signed the agreement to have them move me.  Then "crickets".

So, I was charged almost $1,400 dollars for services not rendered because Lile Moving and Storage did not have the staff or vehicle to provide the service.  NO offer to credit that service only an email explaining how I could file a "claim" with North American Van Lines, even though my agreement for that service was specific to Lile Moving and Storage and their packing service.

After speaking to the GM and the CFO to attempt to get some resolution, they only hid behind their contract language.

The GM (Erik Grimaldo) initially offered to honor the original estimate on the packing materials portion in an effort to 'make things right'. But the CFO (Vanessa Rimby)then vetoed that, saying her GM didn't have the authority to make that decision and the company has been quiet ever since and will not respond to phone calls or emails.  Again, just trying to get credit for services NOT provided/rendered.

Additionally, the 'experienced' estimator/salesperson (Casey Limbach) missed his materials estimate by 50% and the weight was off by almost 2000lbs on a light 7,000lb move. 28.5% off, Really???   He came to the house and took pictures of the inventory!

The contracted driver from Humboldt Moving and Storage and his team had to help the one packer that Lile Moving and Storage sent and did NOT receive any payment for that help.

When I say help, the 4 of them packed almost 1/2 of the house in 1.5 hours after the packer from Lile spent 6 hours in 2 rooms. I even provided materials to the packer from what I had because he didn't have what he needed. As a matter of perspective, the house was only 1650 sqft with only one 10' long closet of clothes.
I then had to clean up the tape, paper, trash, broken decor, etc without so much as a simple apology from the packer that Lile Moving and Storage sent.

To be clear, I am not looking to receive a credit for services I received or wasn't happy with, I'm trying to just get a credit for services I DID NOT receive by Lile Moving and Storage. Seems simple enough, but apparently it's not.

I understand contracts, but I also understand accepting responsibility/accountability for mistakes, poor planning, poor staffing, poor communication and poor customer service.

Lile Moving and Storage has purposely chosen not to accept any responsibility for any of these, but has chosen to hide behind "the contract" and not accept any responsibility.

Their behavior and lack of willingness to engage in a conversation only solidifies my belief that this a standard, malicious, deceitful and directed practice for Lile Moving and Storage. Based on my interactions it seems to start at the top and supported by the entire group.

Had it not been for Art, the driver and his team from Humboldt Moving and Storage, (Highly Recommend)  the move would have been disastrous.
AI generated response, responder doesn't exist at Lile.
Spoke with Evan on 3/18, he confirmed there is no "Lori S"/ Business Manger at Lile that he could find in the company directory. He took my email, said he would contact Vanessa Rimby to call me back and copy me on the email request to do so. I've sent 3 email & 3 calls in 2 weeks
No response from anyone thus far.","Images":null,"When":"Edited a year ago"},{"Name":"Tomeka Houle","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocJRFG6OiCm_ca9nevzwWwevpnsePDRDvpnL7POYjB5mkVZObw=s120-c-rp-mo-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"I had an amazing experience with Lile North Moving & Storage Vancouver, WA. They were absolutely awesome from start to finish. Over the course of four full days, the team was always on time, extremely professional, and incredibly well-organized.

A special shoutout to Darmarvis Lee and Montoris Boyd—they were outstanding! Their teamwork, attention to detail, and respect for my belongings made the entire process smooth and stress-free.

If you’re looking for a reliable, efficient, and courteous moving company, Lile is the one to call. I couldn’t recommend it more. We’ve been able to flex our space up based on our seasonal demand, which is impossible elsewhere (we tried). The dock is large, and all our shipments get received successfully without us being there. It’s a game changer to have daily (late afternoon) pick ups from all the major carriers, allows us to ship to all customers same day they order without running all over town.

The site manager is very helpful and competent in every way, goes above and beyond for us every day.

Bathrooms are clean, meeting areas are spread out all over, generally quiet in the warehouse so it’s easy to work. Conference room is available for a low fee, which is great, when it was free it was never available as people camped out in there.

Over all very happy with Portal, they have allowed our company to feel supported as we grow!","Images":null,"When":"5 months ago"},{"Name":"Jill Lloyd","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjUfhHqU1ACflrqBbCgVNcOeTXHArbx46DNgMeQRUCJxbRPfxp29=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":1,"Description":"My experience with Portal Warehouse has been the most high-conflict and disappointing business relationship I have ever encountered.

I would not recommend this space to any business owner who values stability, transparency, professionalism, or predictable operating terms.

One of the biggest concerns is that you are not treated as a traditional tenant with a standard Minnesota lease. You are considered a “member.” In my experience, that distinction matters. It appears to give Portal far more power to manipulate than a traditional lease arrangement would, while leaving the business owner with fewer practical protections than they may expect when renting commercial space in Minnesota.

In my experience, Portal can create, implement, reinterpret, or modify fees, charges, rules, services, access, delivery practices, and other operating terms without meaningful agreement from the member. That kind of arrangement creates real risk for a business owner who needs consistency in order to serve clients, receive deliveries, plan staffing, manage expenses, and operate professionally.

When a company can change the rules and then simply claim it has the right to do so, the relationship no longer feels like a true partnership. It feels one-sided.

My experience has included shifting expectations, inconsistent enforcement, poor communication, unexpected changes, and a lack of accountability when concerns were raised. I felt dismissed, financially taken advantage of, and treated as though Portal’s interpretation of the agreement was the only one that mattered.

I do not write negative reviews lightly. As a business owner myself, I understand how much reviews matter. But other business owners deserve to know what they may be walking into before signing anything.

Based on my experience, I could not in good conscience recommend Portal Warehouse to another business owner.","Images":null,"When":"a month ago"},{"Name":"Brian Dillon","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocIhLfSRPP7jjZIOkYPDh-PJtwf0yz0RB4fnbhi3ToTIr8DgJQ=s120-c-rp-mo-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"We came across Portal Warehousing when we were searching for our company's first space. After six months, we can confidently say we made the right choice.

For a small business, many amenities present at Portal would be unattainable had we leased a traditional single space. Having access to a kitchen, conference room, working spaces and a large dock to support shipments has supported our team and company's growth. The space is kept clean and amenities in good working order.

The onsite property support staff is fantastic. Very responsive, clear communication about site happenings, and we were welcomed in and set up for success.","Images":null,"When":"5 months ago"},{"Name":"Midori Von Bargen","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjVvaE13gNVIPSPebp7kn5hQ2lUQJD6Z0SBLzT5aYjGj-LRxJgi-sg=s120-c-rp-mo-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"We’ve had a great experience working out of this co-warehouse space. The facility is clean, well-organized, and thoughtfully designed for growing businesses that need flexibility and room to scale. The amenities are a huge plus — from complimentary energy drinks and easy printing access to reliable package pickup and delivery Monday through Friday, everything is set up to make day-to-day operations run smoothly.

Inc.","Images":null,"When":"2 years ago"},{"Name":"Drew Lederman","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjWDu9P4vHYV8MVjHZm0cvIMp2EOXplzRUADw5zTwdinDW_2WXfM=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"I had been at ReadySpace for almost a year before my business moved into a 3PL — now I feel like I can give a full review!

I started out with around 125 sqft for our packing and shipping. It was perfect for our needs at the time, and when we outgrew it, we moved into around 250 sqft.

My favorite things about ReadySpaces:
- If you have a window, you get great views of the city
- UPS picks up every day!
- There are communal carts and pallet jacks (which are first come first serve)
- The 4th floor has a lounge to put your lunch in the fridge and heat it!
- The warehouse can grow with you — as you grow you can rent larger spaces.
- Everyone is SO nice. So many other tenants have helped us out in our time there with loading up vans and using the pallet jacks. I have never met more helpful or kind people. Lots of small businesses which makes a great community!

Things to note:
- It’s dusty! Unavoidable!
- Sometimes the frieght elevators are in use by other tenants which can delay things
- Sometimes the loading dock is occupied or someone parked in front of the loading dock when you need it — it’s a shared space so be aware that you need to be patient
- You have to be clean! There are dumpsters and loading docks in the front. And you will be fined for leaving pallets or trash out.
- Sometimes the bathroom doesn’t have toilet paper or soap. When this happens I go to one of the other bathrooms!

All in all, I enjoyed my time at ReadySpaces and am so happy we found it since there is nothing else like it in the area. Thank you again to Danielle for making our time there great!","Images":null,"When":"2 years ago"}]

Highly recommend!","Images":null,"When":"a year ago"},{"Name":"Will Iam","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjXwtmbwvGfEu3F2X8axjycr0QDzOFS7XT44Fyx7rHIg9srNazc=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":1,"Description":"Extremely Disappointing Experience – Unprofessional Conduct and Poor Communication

Our experience with Saltbox has been extremely disappointing from start to finish. Ms. Lynn Osei, who served as our primary point of contact, was consistently unpleasant and unprofessional in her interactions. Multiple members of our team independently noted how unwelcoming and uncooperative she was throughout the process.

Due to an urgent operational need, Saltbox was the only option that could accommodate our short-term requirements. Otherwise, based on the customer service alone, we would not have considered moving forward.

During our decision-making process, the unit we were interested in was suddenly no longer available—this critical update was not proactively communicated to us. I had to follow up myself to learn that a comparable unit would not be available for another month. Despite the inconvenience, our team agreed to make it work.

We also had to advocate for ourselves to receive the advertised “1-month free” promotion, which was not mentioned at any point during the tour or initial communications. Only after I provided a screenshot from Saltbox’s own corporate website was the promotion acknowledged and included in our agreement.

I executed the lease agreement in a timely manner and understood that, prior to move-in, we needed to submit:

A one-month deposit

A copy of our business license (which required time to obtain, as we are a new business)

Proof of insurance coverage

Instead of collaborating with us to complete the process, we were contacted only after the payment due date with a message implying that the unit would soon be made available to another party. There was no inquiry about the status of the remaining required documents, nor any indication of flexibility. I replied promptly, reiterating that we were working within the agreed-upon timeline—especially considering our lease was not scheduled to begin for another two weeks. I received no response.

Today, we were informed via email that our lease had been canceled due to non-payment and that neither I, my associates, nor anyone affiliated with our business would be permitted to lease from Saltbox at any location moving forward. This decision, made without discussion or accommodation, is both unprofessional and unacceptable.

Moreover, the condition of the warehouse itself was substandard, with one of the bay doors non-functional during our tour.

We will be escalating this matter to the Mayor’s office and the State Attorney General, where we maintain active professional relationships. The disregard for basic business courtesy and contractual fairness exhibited in this case warrants further scrutiny.

We provided a quote, which was approved. Through a third-party representative, our arrival was confirmed with AllSouth. We gave advance notice, three hours, and again when we were one hour out. Both were acknowledged.

To finish the job before their 4 PM closure, we arranged for a rental company to deliver a forklift. This was the first time either our company or the rental provider had worked at this facility. Still, we approached the job with professionalism, clear communication, and full documentation.

The rental driver, a former Marine and highly professional, arrived and was immediately met with hostility. The owner of AllSouth came outside and began shouting and cussing at him, without any conversation or clarification. When the driver politely asked to speak civilly, the owner shouted, “This is a free country.” The driver shut the door and called his supervisor.

We arrived minutes later. A warehouse manager called the owner and put him on speakerphone. The owner, unaware, began the conversation with “Is it [our company]?” and falsely claimed no one informed them we were coming, even though we had proof. He added, “[Our company] doesn’t know how to do their job.” We were told he would speak with us directly. He never did, even after two hours of waiting.

Then we were told we needed a COI, which had never been mentioned before. However, most COI's need around 24 to 48 hours ahead of time to update and approve the policy for a particular customer. We got started immediately, as we always carry proper insurance.

Later, we found out the real reason behind the hostility. There was a personal issue between the warehouse owner and the owner of the rental company. That had absolutely nothing to do with us. The rental driver didn’t even know about it. Instead of handling it professionally, the owner took it out on an unrelated worker, the rental company driver.

We were repeatedly asked how we planned to do the job, even though no one ever reviewed our plan, asked what we brought, or looked at our equipment. Despite all this, they still wanted us to return the next week. But we no longer felt safe or respected. We could not risk being falsely blamed for damage or exposed to more aggression. So we walked away.

Before we could even inform them of our decision, they told us to remove the rental forklift as it could not remain while we waited on the COI's approval. They never agreed to let it stay, but after repeated delays and poor communication, you would think they would try to accommodate us, if not out of professionalism, then at least to retain our business. Instead, we were left covering additional costs and wasted time.

As the owner of my own company, I have had to own up to my mistakes, not through email, and not through a subordinate, but face to face, man to man, as greater men before me have. That is not easy, but it is the right thing to do.

If you're looking for a company that holds itself to high standards, then avoid this company. They will abide by no such morals.","Images":null,"When":"a year ago"}]
